si4_title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

dc1_datasets_using.detail: The study used a single-site dataset consisting of 98 first-episode drug-naive OCD patients and 130 healthy controls recruited from the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University.
dc1_datasets_using.supporting_text: Ninety-eight first-episode and drug-naive patients with OCD were recruited from outpatient services of the Department of Psychiatry, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University. ... One hundred and thirty healthy controls (HCs) were recruited from the community through poster advertisement.

answer.SINGLE-SITE: normative training/testing, patient for clinical research

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The healthy control (HC) group was used to train the normative model (Gaussian process regression). The patient group was used to derive individualized neuroanatomical differences and parse them into disease factors using non-negative matrix factorization.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs and then applied the trained model to infer GMV of patients with OCD.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling latent disease factors
